alternatives.root_cause: A runtime flag was flipped in the flag store, enabling a recommendation code path that fails or leaks, with no artifact or config change recorded.
alternatives.why_not: The change logs for both recommendation and flagd are empty as this class predicts (tr_8edbbe078f9f, tr_145bd22a70ef), but flagd produced no log lines at all in the window (tr_e20158cf6250) and no flag evaluation changed behaviour in the traces, so there is no positive evidence of a flip; a flip is also a plausible trigger for the same exhaustion rather than a competing mechanism.

alternatives.root_cause: product-catalog became slow under traffic shaping and recommendation failed while waiting on it.
alternatives.why_not: product-catalog's error ratio is flat zero (tr_718779b87cee), its spans in the sampled traces complete in single-digit milliseconds (tr_31a1e623c034), and every traffic-shaping attachment in its change history was removed hours before onset (tr_b2b625132003).

alternatives.root_cause: The recommendation process froze while its socket kept accepting, hanging callers to their deadlines.
alternatives.why_not: A frozen process writes nothing, but recommendation kept emitting log lines throughout the window (tr_5c4a0f75067a), and the frontend saw fast connection resets rather than deadline hangs (tr_e35b1e6379d8).

verdict.summary: The recommendation service intermittently stops serving and drops in-flight gRPC connections - consistent with its process being killed and restarted after exhausting memory - so callers see resets and the recommendation path shows traffic gaps rather than steady errors.
verdict.reasoning: recommendation's error ratio never departs from baseline but roughly half the intervals in the incident window have no defined value at all, i.e. intervals with no traffic (tr_442550895c67); its own log shows request handling ceasing well before the window closes while only exporter failures continue (tr_5c4a0f75067a), and its traces stop appearing after the early part of the window (tr_31a1e623c034). The frontend records gRPC UNAVAILABLE connection-reset failures, including one wrapped by a Python application reporting its own reset downstream (tr_e35b1e6379d8), which is the shape of a callee dying mid-call rather than returning errors. product-catalog, the only shared downstream on that path, is clean on error ratio (tr_718779b87cee) and silent in logs (tr_f9e99c52c7af), and its only recorded changes are traffic-shaping attachments hours before onset that were all removed (tr_b2b625132003), so a slow dependency does not explain the gaps. No deploy or config change landed on recommendation (tr_8edbbe078f9f) or flagd (tr_145bd22a70ef), so the failure is in the running process rather than in a new artifact or edited value; repeated disappearance-and-return of a service with no change behind it is the signature of the process being killed for over-consuming a resource. frontend-proxy's edge error ratio moved only slightly (tr_e98e6975a937), consistent with it being the noticer, not the breaker.
open_questions: No memory, CPU, file-descriptor or restart-count metric was retrieved for recommendation, so exhaustion is inferred from traffic gaps and resets rather than observed directly.
Which resource was exhausted, and whether the kill was an OOM kill or a liveness-probe restart, is unsettled.
The log result elided the middle of the window, so the exact first moment recommendation stopped serving relative to the 13:13:31 onset is not pinned down.
flagd wrote no logs in the window, so a runtime flag flip into a leaking code path could not be confirmed or excluded.
frontend-proxy and load-generator produced no logs, leaving the caller-side timeout-versus-reset distinction unverified at the edge.
